newsitem.title: USA: IMM mark and Swiss franc futures close near highs.
newsitem.headline: IMM mark and Swiss franc futures close near highs.

text.p: IMM mark and Swiss franc futures closed higher, reversing a weak opening after the U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book left the impression the Fed would not raise U.S. rates at the end of March, market sources said.
The book on U.S. economic activity described price pressures as "temperate," and said wage gains remained moderate despite tight labor markets.

June marks jumped to $0.5948, and should probe resistance at $0.5953 on GLOBEX, or about 1.69 spot marks. June Swiss francs climbed to $0.6953, through resistance at $0.6942, on dampened expectations for a U.S. rate hike on March 25.
However, traders said the book confirmed the long-term bullish trend for the dollar against most foreign currencies.
"You still have the same argument," one trader said.
"The market is set up for long term gains, but you have to have some new impetus," another trader said about the dollar's inability to re-test the upper end of its recent range.

"Unless we got something radically different, I don't think the dollar will do much," one currency analyst said, adding that the dollar/mark would be well within its ranges if it fell to 1.69 spot rate overnight.

Traders and analysts said activity was extremely quiet, with pit trade consisting mostly of spread trading out of the March contract and into June. The last trading day for March currency contracts is on Monday, March 17.
Market speculation that there would be a delay in the European Monetary Union (EMU) initially led June marks through resistance at $0.5912 to $0.5914 at midsession, pit traders said.
After June marks popped higher, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said there was no doubt that the EMU would start as planned January 1999.
But mark futures continued to rise amid dollar profit-taking.
"It's been very technical," one forex broker said about the dollar's selloff. "There were a lot of stop losses."
He said dollar/mark held a firm tone at the opening on talk an European central bank was selling marks for lira.
Yen and sterling futures trimmed losses, with June yen trading up to $0.008292, or about 122.25 spot yen.
Traders and analysts said the market would closely focus on U.S. February retail sales on Thursday and the U.S. February Producer Price Index (PPI) on Friday.

Sales, which will be released at 0830 EST/1330 GMT on Thursday, are forecast to rise 0.6 percent, versus up 0.6 percent in January, and excluding autos, sales are seen rising 0.7 percent, versus a gain of 0.4 percent in January.
Overall PPI is forecast to fall 0.1 percent, compared to down 0.3 percent in January, while the core rate is forecast to rise 0.1 percent, against unchanged in January.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000033 at $0.008288, marks were up $0.0037 at $0.5942, Swiss francs were up $0.0086 at $0.6948, sterling fell $0.0100 at $1.5954, and Can dollars were $0.0020 higher at $0.7381.
